meta.scalability_note: 5 EU regions (Stockholm, London, Amsterdam, Frankfurt, Karlskrona), OpenStack auto-scaling via Heat, managed Kubernetes (Magnum); broader regional footprint than most EU-sovereign providers
meta.performance_note: ISO 27001 certified, 99.9% SLA, EU-only data residency, Swedish Data Protection Act compliance, GDPR-by-design architecture

AWS Amplify.note: No managed frontend or full-stack web application hosting platform. Applications must be self-hosted on VMs or Kubernetes.

AWS Lambda.note: No Function-as-a-Service offering. Serverless compute is not available; workloads require VMs or containerised deployments.

Amazon ECS.note: No managed container runtime service without Kubernetes. Container orchestration is only accessible via the Kubernetes (Magnum) offering.

Amazon EKS.note: Kubernetes clusters provisioned via OpenStack Magnum. Managed upgrades and integrated monitoring are limited compared to fully managed Kubernetes services.

Amazon EC2.note: Flexible VM instances available across all five EU regions. Standard, compute-optimised, and memory-optimised flavors supported via OpenStack Nova.

AWS Batch.note: No managed batch compute service. Batch workloads must be self-orchestrated via VMs or Kubernetes Jobs.

AWS Elastic Beanstalk.note: No PaaS application deployment and lifecycle management platform.

Amazon S3.note: Multi-region S3-compatible object storage with full S3 API support and geo-redundancy options. Available across EU regions.

Amazon S3 Glacier.note: No archival or cold-storage tier. Object Storage operates at a single standard tier with no automated lifecycle archival.

Amazon EBS.note: SSD-backed block volumes with snapshot support and cross-availability-zone replication. Managed via OpenStack Cinder.

AWS Backup.note: VM and volume snapshots are available for scheduled and on-demand use. No unified cross-service backup policy engine or centralised management.

Amazon EFS.note: No managed shared or distributed file system. NFS-based shared storage must be self-hosted.

Amazon RDS.note: Managed MySQL and PostgreSQL via OpenStack Trove. Less mature than RDS; high-availability and multi-AZ failover options are limited.

Amazon DocumentDB.note: No managed document database service. MongoDB or equivalent must be self-hosted.

Amazon DynamoDB.note: No managed NoSQL key-value or wide-column database service.

Amazon Aurora.note: No high-performance distributed relational database equivalent to Aurora.

Amazon ElastiCache.note: No managed in-memory caching service. Redis or Memcached must be self-hosted.

Amazon Redshift.note: No managed cloud data warehouse service.

AWS Application Load Balancer.note: HTTP/HTTPS load balancing with health checks and TLS termination via OpenStack Octavia. Less feature-rich than AWS ALB; advanced routing rules are limited.

AWS Network Load Balancer.equivalent: Cleura Load Balancer TCP mode (OpenStack Octavia)
AWS Network Load Balancer.note: TCP-level load balancing is available via the same Octavia product. Advanced NLB capabilities such as static IPs and protocol-level persistence are limited.

Amazon VPC.note: Full private networking with subnets, routing tables, security groups, and floating IPs. Managed via OpenStack Neutron.

Amazon Route 53.note: Managed DNS service with support for all standard record types across all EU regions. Managed via OpenStack Designate.

Amazon API Gateway.note: No managed API gateway service. API management requires self-hosted solutions such as Kong or NGINX.

Amazon CloudFront.note: No global CDN service. Content delivery requires third-party CDN integration.

AWS Direct Connect.note: Private network connectivity to Cleura data centers is available. Limited self-service provisioning; requires manual engagement with support.

Amazon Rekognition.note: No managed computer vision or image/video analysis service.

Amazon SageMaker.note: No managed machine learning platform for model training and deployment.

Amazon Bedrock.note: No managed generative AI or foundation model API service.

AWS Glue.note: No managed ETL or serverless data integration service.

Amazon EMR.note: No managed big data processing service (Hadoop/Spark). Must be self-hosted.

Amazon Athena.note: No serverless interactive query service for data in object storage.

AWS IAM.note: Project and domain-scoped RBAC with federated identity support and token-based API access. Managed via OpenStack Keystone.

Amazon Cognito.note: No managed user identity and authentication service for applications. Requires self-hosted identity providers (e.g. Keycloak).

AWS IAM Identity Center.note: No centralised SSO or workforce identity management service.

AWS KMS.note: Cryptographic key lifecycle management via OpenStack Barbican. No dedicated HSM service; hardware-backed key storage is not available as a standard offering.

AWS Secrets Manager.note: No managed secrets rotation and storage service. Requires self-hosted solutions such as HashiCorp Vault.

AWS Certificate Manager.note: No managed TLS certificate provisioning or lifecycle management service.

Amazon GuardDuty.note: No managed threat detection or continuous security monitoring service.

AWS Security Hub.note: No managed cloud security posture management or centralised security finding aggregation.

AWS Config.note: No managed resource configuration tracking or compliance evaluation service.

AWS Shield.note: Network-level DDoS protection is included at the data centre perimeter. No application-layer mitigation or WAF-integrated DDoS response.

AWS WAF.note: No managed web application firewall service.

AWS CloudTrail.note: IAM and resource API activity audit logging available via OpenStack. Log retention and export capabilities are limited.

Amazon CloudWatch.note: Basic resource metrics collection via Gnocchi and Ceilometer. Less integrated with platform services and less feature-rich than CloudWatch.

Amazon SNS.note: No managed pub/sub or push notification service.

AWS Systems Manager.note: No managed operational tooling for patching, run commands, or inventory collection.

AWS Cost Explorer.note: Per-project usage and cost reporting available in the customer console. Covers all compute, storage, and networking resources.

AWS CodeBuild.note: No managed CI build service. CI pipelines require self-hosted or third-party tools (e.g. GitLab CI, Jenkins).

AWS CodeDeploy.note: No managed application deployment automation service.

AWS CodePipeline.note: No managed CI/CD pipeline orchestration service.

Amazon ECR.note: Basic OCI/Docker container registry functionality available. Image vulnerability scanning and automated retention policies are limited.

AWS CloudFormation.note: No native infrastructure-as-code service. OpenStack Heat templates provide partial IaC capability; a Terraform provider is also available.

AWS IoT Core.note: No managed IoT connectivity or device messaging platform.

AWS IoT Device Management.note: No managed IoT device registry or fleet management service.

Amazon SQS.note: Basic managed message queue via OpenStack Zaqar. Rarely used in production environments; limited throughput and management features compared to SQS.

Amazon EventBridge.note: No managed event bus or event-driven integration service.

AWS Step Functions.note: No managed serverless workflow orchestration service.

Amazon SES.note: No managed transactional or bulk email delivery service.

Amazon Kinesis.note: No managed real-time data streaming or ingestion service.
